title: Man Utd Player Ratings vs. Atletico Madrid: Wasteful Finishing Undermines Improved Outing
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer5:38 PM EDTMan Utd could not make the most of chances created. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesManchester United are five games without a win in all competitions after suffering a frustrating 2–0 defeat at the hands of Atlético Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday.

The Red Devils ironically put in a much better performance at the Metropolitano in Spain’s capital than the 1–1 draw against Tottenham Hotspur on Sunday, and yet return home to England’s northwest with nothing to show for it.

After the weekend, it was not the start Michael Carrick wanted. World Cup winner Álex Baena raced clear down Atlético’s left flank, the United defense drawn to him, pulling the ball across the box into the path of Pablo Barrios. Ayden Heaven was in the right place to block the shot back across destined for the bottom corner, but the ball still squeezed through.

There was less than one full minute on the clock and Atlético kept looking for similar passes over United’s backline. Still, Bryan Mbeumo went close to an equalizer 12 minutes in, seeing his goal-bound effort deflected wide after a clever nutmeg on Cristian Romero to create the chance. Soon after, Marcus Rashford hoped to do better with an attempted volley.

The visitors had responded positively to falling behind but Jan Oblak was in a good position to deny  Mbeumo and then Carlos Baleba’s free header from the resultant corner, midway through the first half. And yet, Atlético nearly went 2–0 ahead as Álex Grimaldo clipped the angle of post and crossbar with a whipped, curling free kick.

Atlético were even closer to pulling further ahead when USMNT midfielder Johnny Cardoso blasted the ball into the bottom corner, but the goal didn’t survive a VAR review—the ball hit the arm of Marcos Llorente in the immediate build-up.

It was a slower start to the second half until Julián Alvarez struck the post on the volley nine minutes after the restart. Almost straight after, Bruno Fernandes was agonizingly close to converting from Youri Tielemans’s raking pass, guiding the ball just the wrong side of the post.
The captain later struck the bar from distance as the search for an equalizer continued, although substitutions from both managers began to disrupt the flow of the contest.

A VAR review had come to United’s aid in the first half, but Carrick’s team finished the match with 10 players when the referee was advised to take a second look at a battle for the ball between Leny Yoro and Jonathan David. The French defender was harshly penalized for the denial of a goalscoring opportunity when the Canadian tumbled under pressure.

Without Yoro on the field, it took Atlético five more minutes to kill the game off. David was heavily involved, forcing Senne Lammens into a save that offered up a rebound to fellow substitute Ademola Lookman. In the circumstances, there was no way back.
Bryan Mbeumo missed two good chances to score. / Burak Akbulut/Anadolu/Getty ImagesThe outcome of the match hinged on chances that were taken and chances that were not.

Lammens wasn’t as busy as Oblak. Atlético’s early opener was not statistically a ‘big chance’ and, with three-quarters of the match played, the leading hosts hadn’t created one. That was in stark contrast to Manchester United, who made four big chance by that stage of the match and missed all of them. Two fell to Mbeumo, one to Rashford and the other to Fernandes. There is a feeling they probably did enough to win.
But whether more ruthless, or just more confident, Atlético did what the Red Devils couldn’t—find the back of the net.
Andrey Santos made a case for more starts. / Adam Davy/PA Images/Getty ImagesAn improvement in midfield felt like a significant reason for the better performance.

Without the injured Kobbie Mainoo and Fernandes pushed into a wide position, there was opportunity to advance Youri Tielemans into a No. 10 role and line up with a brand-new central midfield pairing: Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos.

This was a less technically-skilled midfield, but one that crucially offered more mobility and a greater physical presence—something United have lacked. Baleba’s integration had been delayed by a preseason injury, while Santos has been a curious omission more often than not. Both will hope this performance will be reason enough to give them more opportunities.
Youri Tielemans was more attacking. / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Senne Lammens—7.0: Not a bad performance despite conceding twice.
RB: Diogo Dalot—6.8: Caught cold by Baena’s run that led to the first-minute opener.
